developments.title: After-hours technology losses coexist with a modest early futures recovery
developments.facts: Public IBD coverage reports renewed technology weakness and Apple falling after earnings. Its original publication was November 2 at 21:53:32 UTC; the observed version was updated November 3 at 00:35:36 UTC. The full early Tuesday Trading Economics narrative reports Apple and Palantir down nearly 3% after hours, while broad US futures edge higher. These are distinct measures. Late Monday Reuters explicitly says technology-investment concerns can support USD haven demand. This challenges a blanket claim that US-origin equity stress necessarily weakens the dollar. No private flows or matched Fed repricing are observed.

developments.title: October lending survey shows softer loan demand and targeted credit tightening
developments.facts: The Fed October SLOOS reports unchanged large/mid-market C&I standards, tighter small-firm standards and weaker domestic C&I demand. Commercial real-estate standards tightened and demand weakened. Mortgage demand weakened; consumer standards were mostly unchanged, with stronger credit-card but weaker auto demand. NDFI standards tightened and some refinancing/liquidity demand rose. Responses were due October 5, so this is a lagged survey released now, not a measurement of November lending or a new crisis.

developments.title: Treasury financing estimates resolve the elapsed funding checkpoint
developments.facts: Treasury projects Q4 privately held net marketable borrowing of USD 618 bn, USD 10 bn below August, with unchanged USD 850 bn end-December cash. Excluding the higher opening cash balance, the estimate rises USD 24 bn. Q1 borrowing is projected at USD 800 bn with USD 1 tn end-March cash. November 2 repo acceptance was zero in the morning and USD 2 mn in the afternoon; reverse repo was USD 5.087 bn. The two-year OTC indication is now around 4.61%, slightly above the prior session, so the earlier intraday decline cannot be extended mechanically. November 2 13/26-week bill discount rates were 4.040%/4.150%, bid-to-cover 2.88/2.89. Routine collateral operations and bill awards do not establish QE or exceptional funding stress.

developments.title: US factory expansion strengthens while pricing and hiring components diverge
developments.facts: ISM October PMI rose to 55.5 from 54.5, above the later Reuters survey of 54.5 and TE 54.6. Production was 59.0, orders 55.5 and employment 52.4; prices fell to 75.2 from 77.9 but remain elevated. Inventories returned to expansion and slower deliveries also support the headline, so the full point is not pure final-demand acceleration. Separately S&P final PMI was revised to 54.9 from flash 56.0, versus September 55.9. These surveys retain distinct panels and definitions.

developments.title: US Q3 domestic demand remains strong; monthly core persistence offsets quarterly disinflation
developments.facts: Q3 advance real GDP grew 3.4% at a seasonally adjusted annualised rate, versus Q2 2.2% and the attributed web survey 3.2%; the broker-model forecast was 1.4% and is not consensus. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9%, versus 4.6%, supporting genuine private demand apart from inventories, trade and government. Investment included inventory accumulation and information-processing equipment. Exports fell and imports rose; neither is described as an independent bullish vote. Gross domestic purchases prices rose 3.0% annualised, a different measure from the GDP deflator. Quarterly PCE inflation slowed to 2.1% from 5.0%, core to 2.5% from 3.3%. Separately, September monthly headline PCE rose 0.5%, 3.6% y/y; core rose 0.3%, 3.1% y/y. Monthly core matched the 0.3% web survey but exceeded the 0.2% broker forecast. August monthly core was revised from 0.2% to 0.3%. Personal income rose 0.2%, nominal spending 0.5%, real spending less than 0.1% (rounded 0.0%), real disposable income fell 0.3%, and saving rate was 3.8%. August income is now 0.3% and real spending 0.5%; original vintages remain preserved. Strong quarterly private demand and revised monthly core persistence oppose the slower quarterly inflation and softer September household real-income/spending figures. One combined package, not a count of components.
